records.speaker: Angelo Puccini
records.Japanese: 提督、ヌケニンって何だい？
records.current_English: Admiral, what's a nukenin?

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese: ヌケニン？
records.current_English: A nukenin?

records.speaker: Yukihisa Shiraki
records.Japanese: もともと忍者だった者のことですな
records.current_English: Someone who used to be a ninja.

records.speaker: Angelo Puccini
records.Japanese:
へー、ニンジャね！
…で、ニンジャって何だい？
records.current_English: A ninja! So... what's a ninja?

records.speaker: Yukihisa Shiraki
records.Japanese:
日本にいる
隠密行動を得意とする一族にござる
records.current_English:
They're from a clan in Japan 
 that specializes in working unseen.

records.speaker: Angelo Puccini
records.Japanese:
うーん、ジャパニーズ・スパイって
ことだな
で、会ったことはあんのかい？
records.current_English:
Japanese spies, then.
 Have you ever met one?

records.speaker: Yukihisa Shiraki
records.Japanese:
いや、一度も
正体を見られた者は死というのが
忍びの掟ゆえ…
records.current_English:
Never. A ninja whose true identity 
 is discovered must die. Such 
 is their code...

records.speaker: Angelo Puccini
records.Japanese: マンマミーヤ！
records.current_English: Mamma mia!

records.speaker: Yukihisa Shiraki
records.Japanese:
もちろん、忍びから足を洗うは命がけの
所行。一族の追撃を振り切った
抜け忍とは、尋常ならざる腕前の
忍者でありましょう
records.current_English:
Leaving a ninja clan 
 can cost you your life.
 A nukenin who escapes pursuit
 must be extraordinarily skilled.

records.speaker: Yukihisa Shiraki
records.Japanese: その抜け忍が、どうか致したか？
records.current_English: Why ask about a nukenin?

records.speaker: Angelo Puccini
records.Japanese:
ああ。っていうより
その衣装のことをちょっと小耳に
はさんだんだ
records.current_English:
Well, I heard something
 about their outfit.

records.speaker: Angelo Puccini
records.Japanese:
真っ黒な服で、『抜け忍の黒装束』と
呼ぶらしいんだ
しかも、服ではなく、防具なんだとよ
records.current_English:
It's a renegade ninja's
 all-black outfit.
 They call it Ninja Garb. It's
 supposed to be armor.

records.speaker: Yukihisa Shiraki
records.Japanese: 防具？
records.current_English: Armor?

records.speaker: Angelo Puccini
records.Japanese:
詳しいことは分かんないが
とっても軽くて、丈夫な物なんだってさ
records.current_English:
I don't know the details,
 but they say it's incredibly light 
 and tough.

records.speaker: Yukihisa Shiraki
records.Japanese:
ほう、そんな物があったとは
初耳だな
records.current_English:
That's the first I've heard
 of such a thing.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
日本人のユキヒサでも
知らないくらいの物なのか…
records.current_English:
Even Yukihisa hasn't heard 
 of it, and he's Japanese...

records.speaker: Yukihisa Shiraki
records.Japanese: いや、面目ない
records.current_English: My apologies.

records.speaker: Angelo Puccini
records.Japanese:
ユキヒサが謝ること
ないじゃないか
records.current_English: No need to apologize.

records.speaker: Yukihisa Shiraki
records.Japanese: しかし…
records.current_English: But...

records.speaker: Angelo Puccini
records.Japanese:
だいたい、俺が言い出したことなんだし
まったく、ユキヒサは面白いね
records.current_English:
I'm the one who brought it up. 
 You're a funny one, Yukihisa.

records.speaker: Yukihisa Shiraki
records.Japanese:
面白い？
…面白いとはどういうことだ
侮辱するのであれば容赦せんぞ
records.current_English:
Funny? What do you mean by that? 
 If you mean to insult me,
 do not expect mercy.

records.speaker: Angelo Puccini
records.Japanese: へえ、どう容赦しないんだい？
records.current_English:
Oh? What are you going 
 to do about it?

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
２人ともやめろ
ケンカをするようなことじゃ
ないだろう
records.current_English:
Both of you, stop. This isn't
 worth fighting over.

records.speaker: Yukihisa Shiraki
records.Japanese: …面目ござらん
records.current_English: My apologies.

records.speaker: Angelo Puccini
records.Japanese:
すまねえ
悪かったよ
records.current_English: Sorry. My fault.

records.speaker: Yukihisa Shiraki
records.Japanese:
…それにしても…
その黒装束とかいう防具
あるとすれば間違いなく
日本でしょう
records.current_English:
Still, if that black armor exists, 
 it must be in Japan.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese: おそらくな
records.current_English: Probably.

records.speaker: Angelo Puccini
records.Japanese:
俺も、そう思うな
暇があったら探してみようぜ
records.current_English:
That's what I think, too. Let's
 look when we have some time.

rows: They call it Ninja Garb. It's

records.speaker: Port Worker
records.Japanese:
おっ
あんたたち、琥珀（コハク）を
扱ってんのかい？
records.current_English: Oh, you trade amber?

records.speaker: Charles Rochefort
records.Japanese:
ええ、そうですよ
…琥珀の輝きを見ていると
太古の時代に誘われるようですね
records.current_English:
We do. When I look at amber's glow,
 I feel drawn 
 into the distant past...

records.speaker: Port Worker
records.Japanese: んん？　何言ってんだ？
records.current_English: Huh? What are you talking about?

records.speaker: Charles Rochefort
records.Japanese:
琥珀というのは大昔の樹液が固まって
宝石として生まれ変わった
ものなんですよ
records.current_English:
Amber is resin from ancient trees, 
 hardened and reborn as a gemstone.

records.speaker: Charles Rochefort
records.Japanese:
ほら、この琥珀の中に蜂が見える
でしょう？　この蜂は何千年もの間
セピア色をした小宇宙の中で
眠っているのです。神秘的ですねえ…
records.current_English:
See the bee in this amber? It's
 slept for thousands of years 
 in a little sepia world. 
 How mysterious...

records.speaker: Port Worker
records.Japanese:
はあ？　兄ちゃん、なんで
そんな小難しいこと知ってんだよ
records.current_English: How do you know all that?

records.speaker: Charles Rochefort
records.Japanese:
科学の力です。科学というものは
人智を越えたこの世の奇跡を
人智によって少しでも解き明かそうと
する学問なんですよ
records.current_English:
Science. It uses human reason
 to shed a little light on
 the wonders of the world, even 
 the ones we can't yet explain.

records.speaker: Port Worker
records.Japanese:
？？？　何だかさっぱり分かんねえや
…おっ、そうだ
琥珀といや思い出したことがある
records.current_English:
That went right over my head. Oh,
 speaking of amber...

records.speaker: Charles Rochefort
records.Japanese: 何ですか？
records.current_English: Of what?

records.speaker: Port Worker
records.Japanese:
この岬の沖に、島がいくつかあるんだが
聞いたところによるとその島の中に
琥珀色に輝く不思議な場所が
あるって話だ
records.current_English:
A few islands lie off this cape. 
 They say there's a strange spot on 
 one that glows like amber.

records.speaker: Charles Rochefort
records.Japanese: 琥珀色に？　鉱脈か何かかな？
records.current_English:
It glows like amber? Maybe it's
 a mineral vein...

records.speaker: Port Worker
records.Japanese:
さあね。それが何かってことまでは
分かんねえよ
ま、あくまで噂だしな
records.current_English: No idea. Only a rumor.

records.speaker: Charles Rochefort
records.Japanese:
ふーん、そうですか
わざわざ教えてくれてありがとう
私の科学的好奇心に訴える情報ですよ
records.current_English:
I see. Thanks for telling me.
 You've piqued
 my scientific curiosity.

rows: See the bee in this amber? It's
It glows like amber? Maybe it's

records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.Japanese: ふぅ…
records.current_English: Sigh.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese: じいさん、どうしたんです？
records.current_English: What's wrong, sir?

records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.Japanese: いや、孫のことが心配でな
records.current_English: I'm worried about my granddaughter.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese: クリスティナのことか…
records.current_English: Cristina...

records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.Japanese:
ちゃんとやっておるか、気になるのじゃ
親バカ、いや爺バカと笑うてくれい
records.current_English:
I keep wondering how she's getting 
 on. Call me a doting parent... 
 er, grandfather.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
クリスティナのことなら、心配は
無用でしょう。彼女は、並みの男よりも
ずっとしっかりしている
まるでアテナの生まれ変わりだ…
records.current_English:
Don't worry about Cristina.
 She's more capable than most men.
 She's like Athena reborn...

records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.Japanese: アテナ？
records.current_English: Athena?

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
ローマ神話でいうところの
ミネルヴァのことです
records.current_English: The Romans called her Minerva.

records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.Japanese:
むかーしに、聞いたような気もするが
神さんの話ってのはよう知らんのじゃ
records.current_English:
I may have heard that long ago,
 but I don't know much about
 the gods.

records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.Japanese:
…しかし、そのミネ何とかってのは
聞いたような気がするな
records.current_English:
Still... I feel I've heard 
 that Min-something name before.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
とにかく、クリスティナのことは
心配いりませんよ
records.current_English:
Anyway, you don't have to
 worry about Cristina.

records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.Japanese:
…ありがたいのう
クリスティナは提督に信頼されておるの
じゃな。だが、わしにはただの孫娘じゃ
年寄りの気持ちも分かってくれ
records.current_English:
I'm grateful you 
 trust her, Admiral. To me, she's 
 still my granddaughter. Try to see 
 it from an old man's side.

records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.Japanese:
…おお！
そうじゃ、思い出した！
records.current_English: Ah! Now I remember!

records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.Japanese:
そうじゃ、そうじゃ、たーしか
『ミネルヴァの盾』とか言うとったぞ
records.current_English:
Yes, yes! I think they called
 it the Minerva Shield.

records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.Japanese:
地中海じゃったか、黒海じゃったか…
その辺りに眠っとると噂になった
伝説の防具じゃ。今までは
本気で探しはしなかったが…
records.current_English:
A legendary piece of armor,
 said to lie somewhere
 around the Mediterranean.
 Or was it the Black Sea? 
 I never looked for it
 in earnest, but...

records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.Japanese:
クリスティナがミネルヴァのようだと
聞いたらすごく手に入れたくなったわい
本当にあるんならクリスティナに
持たせてやりたいのう…
records.current_English:
You say Cristina's like Minerva? 
 Now I really want to find
 that shield. If it's real, 
 I'd like her to have it...

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese: じいさん…
records.current_English: Sir...

records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.Japanese:
くだらん話をして悪かったの
爺のたわ言だと思うて、忘れてくれい
さ、そろそろ仕事に戻らんとな
records.current_English:
Sorry for rambling. Forget the old 
 man's nonsense. I'd better 
 get back to work.

records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.Japanese: ほれ、提督も仕事をせんと
records.current_English: You too, Admiral.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese: ああ…そうですな
records.current_English: Yes...

rows: trust her, Admiral. To me, she's
still my granddaughter. Try to see
it from an old man's side.

records.speaker: Samwell Khan
records.Japanese: 提督、ちょっといい？
records.current_English: Admiral, a moment?

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese: 何だ
records.current_English: Hm?

records.speaker: Samwell Khan
records.Japanese:
孔雀っていう、世にも美しい鳥が
いるんだけどさ、見てみたいよね
records.current_English:
Peacocks are such beautiful birds. 
 Wouldn't you love to see one?

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
いったい、何の話だ
こいつ…また、何かの噂を
聞いたんだな
records.current_English: What now? Another rumor?

records.speaker: Samwell Khan
records.Japanese:
実はそうなんだよね
『孔雀かたびら』っていうんだけど
records.current_English: Yes. About the Peacock Mail.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
孔雀という鳥の羽を使ったかたびら
とかいうんじゃ、ないだろうな？
records.current_English:
Don't tell me it's armor made
 from peacock feathers.

records.speaker: Samwell Khan
records.Japanese:
惜しーーい！　すごく惜しいよ
実はね、孔雀の尾羽を背に付けた
かたびらなんだ
records.current_English:
Close! So close! It's
 mail with peacock tail feathers
 on the back.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese: …あまり強そうじゃないな
records.current_English: Doesn't sound strong.

records.speaker: Samwell Khan
records.Japanese:
でも、見た目に圧倒されて
敵が思わず立ちすくむんだって
それが最大の効果らしいよ
records.current_English:
They say the sight of it can 
 stop the enemy in their tracks.
 That's supposed to be its
 biggest advantage.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
そ、そうか
それで、どこにあるんだ？
records.current_English: Right... Where is it?

records.speaker: Samwell Khan
records.Japanese:
喜望峰をずうーと、ずうーと、ずうーと
東南に行った小島に在るらしいんだ
それしか分からなかったんだ
records.current_English:
They say it's on a little island 
 far, far, far southeast
 of the Cape of Good Hope. That's 
 all I could find out.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
それだけでは本当に
見当がつかんな
records.current_English: That's hardly enough to find it.

records.speaker: Samwell Khan
records.Japanese:
でも、見てみたいなあ
きっと、見たこともないような
すごいものなんだろうなあ
records.current_English:
I'd still love to see it... I'll 
 bet it's unlike anything I've
 ever seen.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
そうか、とにかく気には留めておこう
期待はするなよ
records.current_English:
All right, I'll keep it in mind. 
 Don't get your hopes up.

records.speaker: Samwell Khan
records.Japanese: 分かってるって
records.current_English: I know, I know.

rows: They say it's on a little island
of the Cape of Good Hope. That's

records.speaker: Priest
records.Japanese:
もしや汝らは
『覇者の証』を探しておる者か？
records.current_English: Do you seek the Proof of Conquest?

records.speaker: Priest
records.Japanese: 私の思い違いか…
records.current_English: Perhaps I was mistaken...

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese: 『覇者の証』とはいったい…？
records.current_English: What is this Proof of Conquest?

records.speaker: Priest
records.Japanese:
…
海を制する者が手にする
とされるもの…
records.current_English:
...They say it passes
 into the hands 
 of the one who rules the seas.

records.speaker: Gerhard Adernkatz
records.Japanese:
海を制する者…
興味深い話ですな
records.current_English:
One who rules the seas...
 An intriguing tale.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
我々の目的に少なからず関連が
あるかもしれん。…もう少し詳しく
教えていただけまいか？
records.current_English:
That may have a great deal 
 to do with our own purpose...
 Could you tell us more?

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese: 何かご存じか？
records.current_English: Do you know anything about it?

records.speaker: Priest
records.Japanese:
…『証』を探し出す道のりは険しい
生半可な心根の者に話すつもりは
ないが、汝らには、その覚悟があると？
records.current_English:
The road to finding the Proof
 is hard. I tell
 only those truly committed.
 Are you prepared for it?

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
海を制する者が持つ、と聞いた以上
それを手に入れるためには
いかなる試練でもいとわぬつもりだ
records.current_English:
If it belongs
 to the one who rules the seas, 
 I'll face any trial to claim it.

records.speaker: Priest
records.Japanese: …よかろう
records.current_English: Very well.

records.speaker: Priest
records.Japanese:
私が知っておるのは、証の地図は
２つの『地図の鍵』を合わせて
初めて役に立つ、ということ
records.current_English:
All I know is that the 
 map to the Proof is useless until
 you bring two Map Keys together.

records.speaker: Priest
records.Japanese:
それぞれの鍵は、そのままでは
何の意味も持たぬ
records.current_English: Each key alone means nothing.

records.speaker: Priest
records.Japanese:
すでに気付いておるかもしれぬが
地図の鍵は各地の遺跡に隠されている
こともあれば、思わぬ人物が
握っていることもある…
records.current_English:
As you may already have realized,
 Map Keys are sometimes hidden
 in ruins, and sometimes held 
 by people you wouldn't expect...

records.speaker: Priest
records.Japanese: 汝に、ひと振りの剣を与えよう
records.current_English: Take this sword.

records.speaker: Priest
records.Japanese:
汝らに課せられた試練を乗り越え
困っている者を助けるがよい
records.current_English:
Overcome the trials before 
 you, and help those in need.

records.speaker: Priest
records.Japanese:
己の欲に囚われず、富を持たぬ者に
与えよ。争いの元凶を封じ、広く平和を
もたらすがよい
records.current_English:
Do not be ruled by greed. Give 
 to the poor, stop strife at its
 source, and bring peace far
 and wide.

records.speaker: Priest
records.Japanese:
では、汝らに
神のご加護があらんことを
records.current_English: May God protect you.

rows: to the one who rules the seas,
I'll face any trial to claim it.

records.speaker: Runtime-selected crew member
records.Japanese: 提督、これを見てください！
records.current_English: Admiral, please look at this!

records.speaker: Runtime-selected crew member
records.Japanese: 提督、これを見て！
records.current_English: Admiral, look at this!

records.speaker: Runtime-selected crew member
records.Japanese: 提督、これを見てくれよ！
records.current_English: Admiral, take a look at this!

records.speaker: Runtime-selected crew member
records.Japanese: 提督、これを見るんじゃ！
records.current_English: Admiral, you'd best look at this!

records.speaker: Runtime-selected crew member
records.Japanese: ていとく、これを見て！
records.current_English: Admiral! Look at this!

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese: ほう、石版か
records.current_English: Oh, a stone tablet.

records.speaker: Gerhard Adernkatz
records.Japanese: 石版が…どうかなさいましたか？
records.current_English:
The stone tablet...? 
 Is something wrong?

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
この辺に石はないゆえ、モスクも泥で
造られているのだ。そこに石版が
あるのは、いかにも不自然だ
records.current_English:
There's no stone around here. They 
 even built the mosque out of mud.
 What's a stone tablet doing here?

records.speaker: Gerhard Adernkatz
records.Japanese:
なるほど！　では…
この石版はよそから持ち込まれたもの！
records.current_English:
I see! Then this stone tablet
 must have been brought here
 from somewhere else!

records.speaker: Speakerless panel
records.Japanese: ひそひそ…
records.current_English: Whisper, whisper...

records.speaker: Bandit
records.Japanese:
困ったことになったな
あれじゃ、とても手が出ねえ…
records.current_English:
We've got a problem. With things 
 like this, there's no way
 we can make a move...

records.speaker: Maria Li
records.Japanese:
…サン＝ジョルジェの街を襲っていた
野盗は、あなたたち？
records.current_English:
Were you the bandits attacking 
 Sao Jorge?

records.speaker: Bandit
records.Japanese:
なっ、なんだ！？
誰だ、てめえは？
records.current_English: W-what?! Who the hell are you?

records.speaker: Maria Li
records.Japanese: FOの者よ
records.current_English: I'm with FO.

records.speaker: Bandit
records.Japanese:
なんだとお！？
あの街の警備に協力なんかしやがって！
こちとら大迷惑だぜ！
records.current_English:
What?! You're the ones 
 helping guard the town! You've 
 made our lives hell!

records.speaker: Bandit
records.Japanese:
てめえのせいで、襲撃できねえ！
メシの食い上げだ！
records.current_English:
Thanks to you, we
 can't raid the town! How 
 are we supposed to eat?!

records.speaker: Xien Yan
records.Japanese:
盗賊の分際で偉そうなことを！
困っている街の住人を放っておく
わけにはいかん！
records.current_English:
That's rich, coming from bandits!
 We won't leave those people
 to fend for themselves!

records.speaker: Bandit
records.Japanese:
うるせえ！
ヤツらヨーロッパ人のおかげで
俺たちの村はメチャクチャに
なっちまったんだ！
records.current_English:
Shut up! Those Europeans wrecked 
 our village!

records.speaker: Bandit
records.Japanese:
誰が何と言おうと
必ず復讐してやる！！
records.current_English: No matter what, we'll have revenge!

records.speaker: Maria Li
records.Japanese:
待ちなさい。あなたたちが恨むべきは
このアフリカで奴隷貿易をする
悪徳商人や掠奪を働く非道な軍人たち
だけでしょう
records.current_English:
Wait. Blame the crooked merchants
 who trade in slaves here in Africa 
 and the ruthless soldiers who
 plunder it.

records.speaker: Maria Li
records.Japanese:
ヨーロッパ人のすべてを憎み
無差別に攻撃するようなら
あなたたちも非道な奴らと変わらないわ
同罪よ
records.current_English:
If you hate every European and 
 strike at random, you're no better 
 than the people who hurt you.
 You're just as guilty.

records.speaker: Bandit
records.Japanese: 聞いた風なことを！
records.current_English: You talk like you know everything!

records.speaker: Maria Li
records.Japanese:
復讐はやめなさい。無意味だわ
あなたたちの幸せを取り戻せるわけ
じゃないでしょう？
records.current_English:
Give up on revenge.
 What good will it do? It can't give
 you back the life you had.

records.speaker: Maria Li
records.Japanese:
そんなことをしても、また争いが
繰り返されるだけ。もっと多くの
あなたの仲間が不幸になるわ
records.current_English:
All it will do is start
 the fighting over again, and more
 of your people will suffer.

records.speaker: Bandit
records.Japanese:
…じゃ、じゃあ
どうしろって言うんだ！
records.current_English: Th-then what are we supposed to do?!

records.speaker: Maria Li
records.Japanese:
とにかく、世界の海で数々の争いの
原因になっている、ヨーロッパ諸国の
勢力争いに終止符を打つことよ
records.current_English:
The European powers' rivalry 
 has caused fighting on 
 seas all over the world. 
 That struggle has to end.

records.speaker: Maria Li
records.Japanese:
世界は全て列強によって分割されようと
しているわ。私たちはそれを阻止する
ため、彼らがその名目として探している
『覇者の証』を集めているの
records.current_English:
The great powers are about 
 to divide the whole world among
 themselves. We're gathering
 the Proofs of Conquest 
 to stop them. They seek them 
 as a pretext for their claims.

records.speaker: Bandit
records.Japanese:
列強を阻止するだと！？
あ…あんたら、正気か？
records.current_English:
Stop the great powers?! A-are
 you out of your mind?

records.speaker: Maria Li
records.Japanese:
はったりで口にできることじゃないわ
このアフリカの地まで勢力圏を広げて
きた以上、私たちも、対等以上に
渡り合う自信はあるわ
records.current_English:
I wouldn't bluff about this. We've 
 extended our reach all the way 
 to Africa. I'm confident we can
 match them, maybe even beat them.

records.speaker: Maria Li
records.Japanese:
どう？　その復讐とやら
私たちに預けてみない？
records.current_English:
What do you say? Will you trust us 
 with your revenge?

records.speaker: Bandit
records.Japanese: なんだって！？
records.current_English: What?!

records.speaker: Maria Li
records.Japanese:
一緒に海に出ましょう
それだけの気概があれば
きっとやれるはずよ
records.current_English:
Come sail with us. With
 that kind of resolve,
 I know you can do it.

records.speaker: Bandit
records.Japanese:
これ以上ここにいても
どうしようもない…
records.current_English: Staying here changes nothing...

records.speaker: Bandit
records.Japanese: よし、あんたに賭けてみよう！
records.current_English:
All right. 
 I'll take a chance on you!

records.speaker: Maria Li
records.Japanese: 歓迎するわ
records.current_English: Welcome.

records.speaker: Bandit
records.Japanese:
あんたの探してるその『証』とやらに
関係あんのかどうかは分かんねえが
遺跡の中に、こんな物が
隠されてたぜ
records.current_English:
I don't know if this has anything
 to do with that Proof you're after,
 but this was hidden in the ruins.

records.speaker: Maria Li
records.Japanese: 石版…？
records.current_English: A stone tablet...?

records.speaker: Benazir
records.Japanese: ねえ、待って
records.current_English: Hey, wait.

records.speaker: Benazir
records.Japanese:
プレゼントをもらいっ放しって
わけにはいかないでしょ
だから、お礼にいいこと教えてあげる
records.current_English:
I can't just take your gift
 and give you nothing in return. Let
 me tell you something useful.

records.speaker: Benazir
records.Japanese:
インドには素晴らしい建物があるの
ここまで来たなら
絶対に訪ねて損はないわ
records.current_English:
There's a magnificent building 
 in India. Since you've come
 this far, it's well worth a visit.

records.speaker: Benazir
records.Japanese:
ただ、地図がないとたどり着けないのが
難点なんだけど。ぜひ行ってみて
records.current_English:
The catch is, you'll 
 need a map to find it. I hope
 you get to see it.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
いいことを聞いた
機会を見つけて出かけてみるよ
records.current_English:
That's good to know. I'll go when
 I have the chance.

rows: need a map to find it. I hope

records.speaker: Diogo Escante
records.Japanese:
おや、これはこれは
FA殿
records.current_English: Well, well. Mr. FA.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese: …俺に何か？
records.current_English: Did you want something?

records.speaker: Diogo Escante
records.Japanese:
残念だが、誰であろうとも
この海域での交易は認められておらぬ
早々に退去せよ
records.current_English:
I'm afraid no one is allowed 
 to trade in these waters.
 Leave at once.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
新大陸での交易に
おまえの許可など必要ないはずだが
records.current_English:
I don't need your permission 
 to trade in the New World.

records.speaker: Diogo Escante
records.Japanese: 分からぬか。では、教えてやろう
records.current_English:
You don't understand? Then allow me
 to explain.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese: 何の用だ？
records.current_English: What do you want?

records.speaker: Diogo Escante
records.Japanese:
そろそろ貸していたカリブ海を
返してもらおうと思ってね
records.current_English:
I thought it was time you returned 
 the Caribbean I lent you.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
貸していた、だと？
どういうことだ？
records.current_English: Lent us? What are you talking about?

records.speaker: Diogo Escante
records.Japanese:
知りたいか？　ふっ…
では、教えてやろう
records.current_English:
You want to know? Heh... Then
 let me explain.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
ディオゴ・デ・エスカンテ…
とうとう本性を現したな
records.current_English:
Diogo de Escante... So you've
 finally shown your true colors.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
我が軍を利用して、宿敵マルドナードを
片づけさせたほどだ、よほどたいそうな
計画を練っていたに違いない
records.current_English:
You used our navy to get rid 
 of your old enemy Maldonado. 
 You must have been planning
 something grand.

records.speaker: Diogo Escante
records.Japanese:
ふっ、なかなか察しがいいな
…教えてやろう
records.current_English:
Heh. You're quite perceptive. Very 
 well, I'll tell you.

records.speaker: Diogo Escante
records.Japanese:
スペインから独立した帝国が
新たに建設される
私はその初代皇帝となるのだよ
records.current_English:
We'll found a new empire 
 independent of Spain. And I'll 
 be its first emperor.

records.speaker: Diogo Escante
records.Japanese:
新大陸一帯はすべて新帝国の版図で
あり、その交易権はすべて帝国に
帰属する。誰であろうと勝手な交易を
認めるわけにはいかぬ
records.current_English:
The new empire will rule 
 the whole New World and hold 
 all its trading rights. No one will
 trade here without our permission.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese: 貴様…！
records.current_English: You...!

records.speaker: Gerhard Adernkatz
records.Japanese: 勝手なことを！
records.current_English: Outrageous!

records.speaker: Diogo Escante
records.Japanese: 目障りだ。さっさと消えてもらおう！
records.current_English:
I've had enough of you.
 Get out of my sight!

records.speaker: Diogo Escante
records.Japanese:
ああ、君たちがダニのような
マルドナードを撃退してくれたことは
感謝している。おかげで独立準備に
専念できたのだからな
records.current_English:
I am grateful you
 drove off that parasite
 Maldonado. That left me free 
 to prepare for independence.

records.speaker: Diogo Escante
records.Japanese:
しかし、もはや用済みだ
さっさと消えてもらおう！
records.current_English:
You've outlived your usefulness. 
 Now get out of my sight!

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
ふん…独立帝国の皇帝とは
大きく出たな。だが、その野望が
成し遂げられる前に騒ぐと、あとで
泣きを見ることになるかもしれんぞ
records.current_English:
So you mean to break away and
 crown yourself emperor? Ambitious. 
 Boast before you've pulled it off
 and you might live to regret it.

records.speaker: Diogo Escante
records.Japanese: 目障りだ。さっさと消えてもらおう！
records.current_English:
I've had enough of you.
 Get out of my sight!

records.speaker: Gerhard Adernkatz
records.Japanese: 提督
records.current_English: Admiral.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese: …ゲルハルトか
records.current_English: ...Gerhard.

records.speaker: Gerhard Adernkatz
records.Japanese:
何度かお呼びしたのですが
お気づきになられなかたので…
records.current_English:
I called a few times,
 but you didn't seem to hear me...

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese: そうだったか、すまんな
records.current_English: You did? Sorry, Gerhard.

records.speaker: Gerhard Adernkatz
records.Japanese: いえ
records.current_English: Not at all.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese: 何かあったのか？
records.current_English: Any trouble?

records.speaker: Gerhard Adernkatz
records.Japanese:
少し気になる報告を受けましたので
お耳に入れておこうかと
records.current_English:
A report caught my attention.
 I thought you should hear about it.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
ゲルハルトが気になるとは
珍しいな
records.current_English:
It caught your attention? That's 
 unusual for you, Gerhard.

records.speaker: Gerhard Adernkatz
records.Japanese:
『善導のステッキ』なる宝物に関する
情報です
records.current_English:
It concerns a treasure called
 the Guiding Staff.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese: 『善導のステッキ』？
records.current_English: The Guiding Staff?

records.speaker: Gerhard Adernkatz
records.Japanese:
そのステッキには、人を善へと
導いてくれるという
言い伝えがあります
records.current_English:
Legend says it guides people toward
 doing good.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
ほう…。だが、ステッキが
人を導くことなど
ありえるのだろうか
records.current_English:
Hm... But how could a staff show 
 someone the right thing to do?

records.speaker: Gerhard Adernkatz
records.Japanese:
たとえ、言い伝えが事実でなくとも
一般にそう信じられている物を
所有するならば、我々の活動の
正しさを世に示すことになりましょう
records.current_English:
Even if the legend isn't true, 
 people believe it. If we had the 
 staff, it would show the world 
 that what we're doing is right.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
そういう考え方もあるか。少なくとも
船員の士気を高めることには
つながるだろうな
records.current_English:
Perhaps. At least it may raise 
 crew morale.

records.speaker: Charles Rochefort
records.Japanese: ちょっと待ってくださいよ
records.current_English: Wait a moment.

records.speaker: Gerhard Adernkatz
records.Japanese: シャルル？
records.current_English: Charles?

records.speaker: Charles Rochefort
records.Japanese:
そんな非科学的ものがなければ
我々のやっていることが正しいって
言えないんですか？
records.current_English:
Since when do we need
 something unscientific to prove
 we're doing the right thing?

records.speaker: Gerhard Adernkatz
records.Japanese: 聞いていたのか？
records.current_English: You were listening?

records.speaker: Charles Rochefort
records.Japanese:
聞こえてきただけです
そんなことより、質問に答えて
ほしいですね
records.current_English:
I happened to overhear. But I'd
 like an answer to my question.

records.speaker: Gerhard Adernkatz
records.Japanese:
我々が軍隊というだけで、各地で無用の
誤解や摩擦が生まれているのだ
このステッキがあれば、不毛な誤解を
招かずにすむかもしれないのだぞ
records.current_English:
Being a military fleet is enough 
 to cause needless
 suspicion and friction 
 wherever we go.
 That staff might spare us some 
 pointless misunderstandings.

records.speaker: Charles Rochefort
records.Japanese:
他の人間がどう思おうと
関係ありませんよ。自分たちが正しいと
信じる道を進んでいるなら
それでいいはずです
records.current_English:
Why care what anyone else thinks?
 As long as we stay on the course 
 we believe is right, that's enough.

records.speaker: Charles Rochefort
records.Japanese:
それとも、我々が正しいってことを
周りの人たちに理解してもらえなければ
気が済まないとでも言うんですか？
records.current_English:
Must everyone agree we're right
 before you're satisfied?

records.speaker: Gerhard Adernkatz
records.Japanese:
おい、どうした、シャルル
何を熱くなっているのだ？
records.current_English:
Charles, what's gotten into you? 
 Why are you so worked up?

records.speaker: Gerhard Adernkatz
records.Japanese:
私は、この艦隊がより円滑に目標に
近づくことが可能な方法を提案した
だけだ。どうなさるかは、提督の
お考え次第だよ
records.current_English:
I merely suggested a way 
 for this fleet to reach its goal 
 with fewer obstacles. The decision 
 is the admiral's.

records.speaker: Charles Rochefort
records.Japanese:
そんなものは必要ありませんよね
提督？
records.current_English: We don't need it, do we, Admiral?

records.speaker: Player choice
records.Japanese: 必要ない
records.current_English: No need

records.speaker: Player choice
records.Japanese: いや、必要だ
records.current_English: We need it

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
そうだな
自分が正しいと信じた道を歩んでいる
以上は、必要のないものだな
records.current_English:
You're right. If we follow 
 the course we believe is right,
 we have no need of it.

records.speaker: Charles Rochefort
records.Japanese: そうですよ
records.current_English: Exactly.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
ゲルハルト
せっかく報告してくれたのに
すまんな
records.current_English:
Sorry, Gerhard. You went to the
 trouble of bringing me that report.

records.speaker: Gerhard Adernkatz
records.Japanese:
いえ、お気遣いなく
さきほども申しましたが
あくまでも私の提案の１つですから
records.current_English:
Please don't concern yourself. 
 As I said, it was only 
 a suggestion.

records.speaker: Gerhard Adernkatz
records.Japanese:
それに、シャルルのこの艦隊に抱く
真摯な思いを改めて知ることが
できました
records.current_English:
Besides, I got to see again
 how much Charles cares 
 about this fleet.

records.speaker: Charles Rochefort
records.Japanese:
いえ、そんな…
私も言い過ぎました
records.current_English: No, I... I went too far.

records.speaker: Gerhard Adernkatz
records.Japanese:
いや、いいのだ
そのまっすぐな気持ちを大切にして
ほしい
records.current_English:
It's all right.
 Don't lose that honesty.

records.speaker: Gerhard Adernkatz
records.Japanese:
それでは、失礼します
行こう、シャルル
records.current_English:
Now, if you'll excuse us... Come 
 along, Charles.

records.speaker: Charles Rochefort
records.Japanese: ええ
records.current_English: Yes.

records.speaker: Speakerless panel
records.Japanese:
FIの精神が
１上がりました！
records.current_English: FI's Spirit rose by 1!

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese: いや、ゲルハルトの言うとおりだ
records.current_English: No. Gerhard is right.

records.speaker: Charles Rochefort
records.Japanese: 提督！
records.current_English: Admiral!

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
シャルルの言うことはもっともだが
我々は私設艦隊ではなくあくまでも
王立海軍だ。国を背負っている
records.current_English:
You have a point, Charles. 
 But we're the royal navy,
 not a private fleet. We represent
 our country.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
我々に対する評価は、すなわち国家への
評価。祖国が世界の海に活動の場を
求めるのならば、まずは広く世間に
認めてもらう必要がある
records.current_English:
How people judge us reflects on
 our country. If our homeland 
 is to expand its reach 
 across the world's seas, 
 we must first earn 
 the world's recognition.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese: 分かってくれるな、シャルル
records.current_English: Do you see what I mean, Charles?

records.speaker: Charles Rochefort
records.Japanese:
…確かに
提督のおっしゃるとおりです
すみませんでした
records.current_English:
...Yes. You're right, Admiral. 
 My apologies.

records.speaker: Charles Rochefort
records.Japanese: ゲルハルト…申し訳ない
records.current_English: Gerhard... sorry.

records.speaker: Gerhard Adernkatz
records.Japanese:
気にすることはない。どんな提案に
対しても、いろいろな意見や考え方が
あるのは当然のことだ
records.current_English:
Don't worry about it. People 
 are bound to see a proposal like 
 that differently.

records.speaker: Charles Rochefort
records.Japanese:
そう言ってもらえると
助かりますよ
records.current_English:
I'm glad you see it that way.
 Thank you.

records.speaker: Gerhard Adernkatz
records.Japanese:
提督
すぐにでも探索に出向きますか？
records.current_English: Admiral, shall we search now?

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese: 場所の見当はついているのか？
records.current_English: Do we know where?

records.speaker: Gerhard Adernkatz
records.Japanese: どうやらインド周辺のようです
records.current_English: Somewhere around India, it seems.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese: よく調べたものだな
records.current_English: You've certainly done your research.

records.speaker: Gerhard Adernkatz
records.Japanese:
実は、イタリアの探検家が
発見したのです
records.current_English:
An Italian explorer actually 
 found it.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
それでは、手に入れようが
ないではないか
records.current_English:
Then how are we supposed 
 to get our hands on it?

records.speaker: Gerhard Adernkatz
records.Japanese:
それが、輸送中に敵兵に襲われ
そのステッキもなくしてしまった
らしいのです
records.current_English:
Apparently, enemy soldiers attacked
 him while he was transporting it.
 The staff was lost in the attack.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese: で、その場所がインド周辺ということか
records.current_English:
And that happened somewhere
 around India?

records.speaker: Gerhard Adernkatz
records.Japanese: はい
records.current_English: Yes.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
それ以上詳しくは
分からないのだな
records.current_English: Nothing more precise?

records.speaker: Gerhard Adernkatz
records.Japanese: 申し訳ありません
records.current_English: My apologies.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
探索するにしても範囲が広すぎる
近くまで出向くことがあれば
探してみるとしよう
records.current_English:
The search area is too wide. We'll 
 look if our travels take us nearby.

records.speaker: Gerhard Adernkatz
records.Japanese: 了解しました
records.current_English: Understood.

records.speaker: Charles Rochefort
records.Japanese: 分かりました
records.current_English: Understood.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese: マヌエル、出港準備はできたか？
records.current_English: Manuel, ready to depart?

records.speaker: Manuel Almeida
records.Japanese:
いやあ、提督
今から物資を補給するところですわ
さ、指示をお願いしますよ
records.current_English:
Ah, Admiral. I'm just about
 to take on supplies. What
 would you like us to do?

records.speaker: Player choice
records.Japanese: いいだろう
records.current_English: All right.

records.speaker: Player choice
records.Japanese: おまえに任せる
records.current_English: You handle it.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese: 指示というほどのものでもないだろう
records.current_English:
I don't think you
 need special orders for that.

records.speaker: Manuel Almeida
records.Japanese:
そうですな
補給することを伝えれば
あとは勝手にやってくれますからな
records.current_English:
True enough. Just tell 
 the crew to resupply and 
 they'll do the rest.

records.speaker: Speakerless panel
records.Japanese:
出航前には忘れずに補給して
おきましょう。航行中に食料と水が
なくなると、艦隊が全滅することも
あります
records.current_English:
Always resupply before sailing.
 Running out of food and water
 can destroy the whole fleet.

records.speaker: Speakerless panel
records.Japanese:
通常は最大限まで補給されますが
資金が足りないときは、買える分しか
補給されません
records.current_English:
The crew normally buys as much
as the fleet can carry. If you're 
short on funds, they'll buy only
what you can afford.

records.speaker: Speakerless panel
records.Japanese:
水と食料の補給割合を変えたいときは
いったん補給を断ると
改めて設定できます
records.current_English:
To change the balance of food
 and water, decline resupply first. 
 You can then adjust the amounts.

records.speaker: Manuel Almeida
records.Japanese: はいはい。さっそくかかりますよ
records.current_English: Right, right. I'll get on it.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese: シャルル、戦利品はどうだった？
records.current_English: Charles, how was the haul?

records.speaker: Charles Rochefort
records.Japanese:
なかなかのもんですよ
今、売りさばいているところです
指示をお願いできますか？
records.current_English:
We did pretty well. I'm
 selling the goods now. 
 Want to take over?

records.speaker: Player choice
records.Japanese: いいだろう
records.current_English: All right.

records.speaker: Player choice
records.Japanese: 売らなくていい
records.current_English: Don't sell it.

records.speaker: Speakerless panel
records.Japanese:
交易するときは、『交易』を選び
購入・売却する交易品を選びます
records.current_English:
Choose Trade, then select the goods
 to buy or sell.

records.speaker: Speakerless panel
records.Japanese:
空の船倉があるときだけ購入できます
積み荷があるときは、売却する交易品を
先に決めて船倉をあけます
records.current_English:
You can only buy goods when you
 have an empty cargo hold. If you're
 carrying cargo, choose which goods 
 to sell first to free up a hold.

records.speaker: Speakerless panel
records.Japanese:
売却するときは
十字ボタンで売却する品を選び
Ａボタンを押してください
records.current_English:
To sell, use the D-pad to choose 
 goods, then press A.

records.speaker: Speakerless panel
records.Japanese:
購入するときは
特産品から購入する品を選んで
Ａボタンを押してください
選ばれた特産品が船倉に入ります
records.current_English:
To buy, pick a local specialty 
 and press A. The selected goods go 
 into the hold.

records.speaker: Speakerless panel
records.Japanese:
すべての船で購入・売却する品を
決めたら、『Ｘ完了』を押してください
これで交易交渉は成立です
records.current_English:
Choose what to buy and sell 
on each ship. Then
press X to complete the trade.

records.speaker: Charles Rochefort
records.Japanese:
そうですか
では、このまま積んでおきますね
records.current_English:
All right. We'll keep
 the goods aboard.

records.speaker: Charles Rochefort
records.Japanese: ん？
records.current_English: Hm?

records.speaker: Camille Overijssel
records.Japanese: あ、あの…さっきはすみません
records.current_English:
Um... I wanted to
 apologize for earlier.

records.speaker: Charles Rochefort
records.Japanese:
あ！　例の小娘の！
何しに来やがった！？
records.current_English:
You're the one who 
 was with that brat!
 What are you doing here?!

records.speaker: Camille Overijssel
records.Japanese:
どうしてもみなさんに謝りたくて…
本当にごめんなさい！
あんなひどいこと言うなんて…
records.current_English:
I had to come and apologize
 to all of you... I'm so sorry! 
 She said such awful things...

records.speaker: Camille Overijssel
records.Japanese:
彼女、別にあなたたちを怒らせようとか
いうんじゃないんです
records.current_English: She never meant to anger you.

records.speaker: Camille Overijssel
records.Japanese:
相手をいったん自分の商売がたきって
思っちゃうと
あんな言い方しかできなくて…
records.current_English:
Once she decides someone's 
 a business rival, she just... can't
 seem to talk to them any other way.

records.speaker: Camille Overijssel
records.Japanese:
本当はやさしい娘なんです。ただ
ちょっと、早とちりと思いこみが
激しいっていうか…。どうか
リルを許してやってください！
records.current_English:
She's kind, really. She just 
 jumps to conclusions and gets
 carried away. Please forgive Lil!

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese: …カミル君だったかな？
records.current_English: Camille, was it?

records.speaker: Camille Overijssel
records.Japanese: え？　あ、はい
records.current_English: What? Oh, yes.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
丁重な謝罪、痛みいる
君のような人材がそばにいればこそ
彼女の才覚も活かされているという
ことだろう
records.current_English:
I appreciate your thoughtful 
 apology. With someone as capable 
 as you at her side, she can make 
 the most of her talents.

records.speaker: Camille Overijssel
records.Japanese: い、いえ、そんな
records.current_English: N-no... You're too kind.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
心配は無用だ。我々も敵を選んでいる
君たちに危害を加えたりはせん
帰ったら君の相棒に伝えておいてくれ
records.current_English:
Don't worry. We choose our enemies 
 carefully. We won't harm 
 either of you. Tell her that.

records.speaker: Camille Overijssel
records.Japanese:
あ！　ありがとうございますっ！
…じゃあ、失礼します！
records.current_English:
Oh, thank you so much! Well... 
 I'll be going, then!

records.speaker: Gerhard Adernkatz
records.Japanese: 先行きが楽しみな若者ですな
records.current_English: A promising young man.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
ふむ…
そう言えば、我々の艦隊も
そろそろ人手不足だな
records.current_English:
Hm... Come to think of it, our own 
 fleet is getting short-handed.

records.speaker: Gerhard Adernkatz
records.Japanese:
艦隊を拡充するには
もっと人材が欲しいところですな
records.current_English:
We'll need more capable people 
 if we're to expand the fleet.

records.speaker: Gerhard Adernkatz
records.Japanese:
地中海は海洋貿易立国の多い地域です
リスボンやセビリアなどの大きな都市で
捜せば、有能な者にめぐり会えるかも
しれません
records.current_English:
Many countries around the
 Mediterranean live by sea trade. We
 might find capable people in major 
 cities like Lisbon and Seville.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
そうだな。ついでに、地中海の街々に
航路網を伸ばしておくのもよかろう
records.current_English:
Agreed. It would also be worth 
 extending our trade routes to
 the towns around the Mediterranean.

records.speaker: Guildmaster
records.Japanese: やあ、あんたに紹介したい人がいる
records.current_English:
There's someone I'd like 
 you to meet.

records.speaker: Guildmaster
records.Japanese:
メキシコの総督
ディオゴ・デ・エスカンテ様だ
records.current_English: Mexico's governor, Diogo de Escante.

records.speaker: Diogo Escante
records.Japanese: よろしく
records.current_English: A pleasure.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
ほう…。その総督自らが
俺に何の用だ？
records.current_English:
The governor himself?
 What do you want with me?

records.speaker: Jorge Albacete
records.Japanese:
てめえ、口のきき方に
気を付けやがれ！
records.current_English: Watch your mouth!

records.speaker: Diogo Escante
records.Japanese:
まあよい
君たちに相談したいことがあるのだ
records.current_English:
It's quite all right.
 There's something I'd like 
 to discuss with you.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese: 俺に？
records.current_English: Me?

records.speaker: Diogo Escante
records.Japanese:
君はバスケス・デ・マルドナード
という男を知っているか？
records.current_English: Do you know Vasquez de Maldonado?

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese: …ああ
records.current_English: Yes.

records.speaker: Diogo Escante
records.Japanese:
我々は、ヤツにほとほと
手を焼いている
records.current_English: He has caused us endless trouble.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
…あんたと同じスペイン国籍だったと
思うが？
records.current_English: But isn't he Spanish, like you?

records.speaker: Diogo Escante
records.Japanese:
彼の名目は、空席となった
キューバ総督の代行だが、その実態は
カリブ海一帯をおさえる海賊の
元締めのような男だ
records.current_English:
Officially, he's acting
 governor of Cuba 
 until the vacant 
 post is filled.
 In practice, he's the head 
 of the pirates controlling 
 the Caribbean.

records.speaker: Diogo Escante
records.Japanese:
本国と新大陸を行き来する我々の
商船を配下の海賊どもに次々と襲わせて
おいて、素知らぬ顔でリベートを
吸い上げ、私腹を肥やしている
records.current_English:
He has his pirates attack
 our merchant ships 
 sailing between Spain
 and the New World. 
 Then he pretends to know nothing 
 while pocketing his cut.

records.speaker: Diogo Escante
records.Japanese:
あのハイエナのような男を
早く排除せんと、この海域の
スペイン領の経営は崩壊してしまう
そんなことになったら…
records.current_English:
Unless that hyena is removed 
 soon, Spanish rule 
 in these waters will collapse. 
 And if that happens...

records.speaker: Diogo Escante
records.Japanese:
最近姿を現しはじめたイギリス人
どもに、カリブ海はおろか新大陸全域を
乗っ取られ、スペイン王国の屋台骨
そのものが揺らぐことにもなりかねん
records.current_English:
The English have begun to appear 
 here. They could seize 
 not just the Caribbean,
 but the entire New World.
 It could shake Spain 
 to its foundations.

records.speaker: Diogo Escante
records.Japanese:
そこで君たちと力をあわせて、ともに
あの逆賊を打ち倒したいという
わけなのだ。どうだろうか？
records.current_English:
That's why I'm asking you to 
 join us against that traitor.
 What do you say?

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
今の話が本当なら、彼は立派な
国家反逆罪だ
俺たちの出る幕でもなかろう
records.current_English:
If that's true, he's guilty of high
 treason. Surely you don't need us
 to deal with him.

records.speaker: Diogo Escante
records.Japanese:
明確な証拠がないゆえ、現状では
彼を断罪できない
スペインの同胞に対して、我々から
戦いを仕掛けるわけにもいかん
records.current_English:
We have no conclusive evidence 
 to condemn him. And we cannot
 simply attack a fellow Spaniard.

records.speaker: Diogo Escante
records.Japanese:
我々の代わりに君たちがマルドナードを
駆逐してくれるのであれば
協力は惜しまない
records.current_English:
Drive Maldonado out for us,
 and you will have our full support.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
その結果、俺たちがカリブ海を制圧する
ことになっても構わないと？
records.current_English:
Even if we end up controlling
 the Caribbean?

records.speaker: Diogo Escante
records.Japanese:
輸送船に無差別攻撃を仕掛けるような
男がのさばっているよりは
我々に友好的な勢力がとりしきって
いてくれたほうが、百倍望ましい
records.current_English:
I'd much rather have a friendly
 power in charge than a man 
 who attacks transport
 ships indiscriminately.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
ふっ。イギリスが来るのは困るが
俺たちであればくみしやすいという
ことか
records.current_English:
Heh. You don't want the English
 here, but you think we'll be easier
 to handle.

records.speaker: Diogo Escante
records.Japanese:
…そう、勘ぐらんでもらいたい
ものだな
records.current_English:
I'd prefer you didn't
 read it that way.

records.speaker: Diogo Escante
records.Japanese:
イギリスと本国とは全面的な交戦状態に
ある。おおっぴらにイギリスと
組むことはできん
records.current_English:
Spain is at war with England.
 We cannot openly join the English.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
俺たちも、スペイン王が殺したいほど
憎んでいる新教徒だが？
records.current_English:
We're Protestants too. Wouldn't
 your king gladly see us dead?

records.speaker: Diogo Escante
records.Japanese:
宗教戦争は、ヨーロッパでやって
くれればいい。私としては新大陸にまで
そんな無意味な対立を持ち込む気は
毛頭ない。しかし、イギリスは違う！
records.current_English:
Let Europe keep its religious wars.
 I won't drag that senseless
 conflict to the New World. 
 England is different!

records.speaker: Diogo Escante
records.Japanese:
ヤツらは特別…、スペイン国民の
不倶戴天の敵だ！　この海域にイギリス
王国の国旗がたなびく光景など、想像
するだけでもおぞましいことだよ！
records.current_English:
The English are Spain's sworn
 enemies! The very thought
 of their flag flying over
 these waters disgusts me!

records.speaker: Diogo Escante
records.Japanese:
君たちにとっても損な話ではないと
思うが…。カリブ海進出を狙うので
あれば、マルドナードを相手にしない
わけにもいくまい
records.current_English:
This benefits you as well. If you
 mean to expand into the Caribbean, 
 you'll have to face Maldonado
 sooner or later.

records.speaker: Diogo Escante
records.Japanese:
彼も、海賊あがりの豪腕提督だ
今でも現役で、強力な船団を率いて
いる。君たちの力だけでは
もてあますだろう
records.current_English:
He came up through piracy and he's 
 a formidable admiral. He still 
 commands a powerful fleet. You'd 
 have a hard time facing him alone.

records.speaker: Player choice
records.Japanese: …いいだろう
records.current_English: Very well.

records.speaker: Player choice
records.Japanese: ゲルハルトの考えは？
records.current_English: Gerhard's view?

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
…理屈は分かった
こちらとしても、力を蓄える好機…
records.current_English:
...I see your reasoning. 
 It would give us a chance to build 
 our strength...

records.speaker: Gerhard Adernkatz
records.Japanese:
（…こちらとしても、スペイン領の
　分裂につけこんで、力を蓄える
　好機です。両者を敵にまわすのは
　得策ではありません。）
records.current_English:
(This split in Spain's colonies
 is our chance to gain strength.
 Making both sides enemies
 would be unwise.)

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese: ふむ…
records.current_English: Hm...

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
いいだろう
その話、乗ってみることにする
records.current_English: Very well. We'll accept.

records.speaker: Diogo Escante
records.Japanese:
君が、物分かりの悪い人物でなくて
安心したよ
records.current_English: I'm glad you see reason.

rows: He came up through piracy and he's
have a hard time facing him alone.
